 (Exparte)
 Judgment
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 16.11.2024 at about 2-30 p.m., the petitioner was riding his TVS Star City motorcycle No.KA- 40-L-4761 from Gowribidanur towards Munchenahalli in Bengaluru - Hindura Bypass road and when he reached Hirebidanur Circle,
Gowribidanur Town, at that time the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-MT-9327 came in a rash and negligent manner from opposite direction and dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Gowribidanu Govt. Hospital wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to K.G. Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient.

The petitioner has spent huge amount towards medical expenses,
transportation and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was working as Agriculture and earning sum of Rs.35,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability, the petitioner has lost his income and he has suffered physical and mental stress and frustration.

4. The respondent no.1/the insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-05-MT-9327 has filed the written statement and admitted the Insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no 2 has contended that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident and that petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain and that IMV report indicates no damages was caused to the vehicles allegedly involved in the accident.

It is further contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, who was riding his motorcycle with gear in a rash and negligent manner and unable to control his vehicle, he fallen from the motorcycle and sustained injuries and he was not holding driving license to ride the motorcycle and he was not wearing the helmet and thereby also contributed negligence.
5.
In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.2/ the R.C owner of Car bearing No.KA-05-MT-9327 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES

sentences.text:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 16.11.2024 at about 2.30 p.m., on Bengaluru - Hindura Bypass Road, Hirebidanur Circle, Gowribidanur Town, due to rash ad negligent driving of the driver of car bearing reg.No.KA-05-MT- 9327?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and two witnesses as P.W.2 and PW.3 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P27 and closed evidence on his side.
The respondent no.1 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.1 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle,
P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took on 16.11.2024 at about 2-30 p.m., when the petitioner was riding his TVS Star City motorcycle No.KA-40-L-4761 from Gowribidanur towards Munchenahalli in Bengaluru - Hindura Bypass road and when he reached Hirebidanur Circle, Gowribidanur Town, at that time the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-MT-9327 (hereinafter called as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner from opposite direction and dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to P5 and 9 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint,
spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, wound certificate, charge sheet, Notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon.

12. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Manjunatha Reddy, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.203/2024 of Gowribidanur Town Police Station for the offence punishable under section 125(a), 281 of BNS 2023.
After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 281 and 125(b) of BNS 2023.

sentences.text: By disputing the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident it was vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 by referring the discharge summary as per Ex.P6 that in the Ex.P6 the vehicle which caused the accident was mentioned as two wheeler but not four wheeler hence the alleged offending vehicle which is a Car was not at all involved in the accident.

The learned counsel in further has submitted that in the IMV report, no damage was caused to the vehicles allegedly involved in the accident hence only the petitioner has not produced the IMV report, and on that ground also the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.
The Learned counsel further has argued that since the petitioner was not holding valid driving license and he was not wearing helmet at the time of accident, he has also contributed negligence.

14. In the light of the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.2, if the medical records are perused, it is not in dispute that soon after the accident, petitioner has taken treatment at Govt. hospital Gowribidanur and from there he has taken treatment at K.G. Hospital.
It is true that in the discharge summary as per Ex.P6 issued from K.G hospital, the vehicle involved in the accident was shown as two wheeler.

But, if wound certificate as per Ex.P4 issued from Govt.,
hospital Gowribidanur is perused, wherein the vehicle involved in the accident is shown as Car.
Further, if the MLC and police intimation issued from K.G. Hospital, is perused wherein the alleged H/o RTA is mentioned as 4 wheeler hit to the two wheeler.

The petitioner has produced the letter addressed by him to the K.G. Hospital, stating that, in the discharge summary the vehicle involved in the accident is wrongly shown as two wheeler instead of 4 wheeler.
On the basis of the requisition filed by the petitioner, the discharge summary as per Ex.P14 was issued by correcting the vehicle involved in the accident as four wheeler from two wheeler.

Hence, from the wound certificate issued from Gowribidanur hospital and the MLC and police intimation as per Ex.P17 & 18 issued from K.G.
Hospital and rectified discharge summary as per Ex.P14 it can be gathered that the vehicle involved in the accident was four wheeler but not two wheeler.
It is true that, the petitioner has not produced IMV report.

If really in the IMV report no damage was caused to the vehicle involved in the accident,
then the respondent no.2 could have produced the copy of the IMV report before the court.
Without placing the IMV report, the counsel for R2 submitted that, no damage was caused to the vehicles involved in the accident.
The respondent no.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle has not contested the case.
If really his vehicle was not involved in the accident he could have contested the case.
Hence, the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident cannot be ruled out.

15. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, as per the police records at the time of accident the petitioner was proceeding from Gowribidanur towards Manchenahalli in Bengaluru - Hindupura road.
The offending vehicle which came from opposite direction hit to the vehicle of the petitioner.
As per the evidence of the petitioner he was proceeding on the left side of the road and the offending vehicle which came in a rash and negligent manner hit to his vehicle.
It is true that, the petitioner has not produced the sketch.
But the respondents have not given rebuttal evidence to disprove the police documents and the oral evidence given by the petitioner.

If really the accident in question was occurred in the manner other than the one stated by the petitioner, then nothing prevented the respondents from leading the rebuttal evidence by examining either the driver of the offending vehicle or any independent eye witness.
Hence silence on the part of respondents lend support to the case of petitioner.
Hence, without discussing much on this point this court answers above Issue in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are at Ex.P.4, P6 and 14.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at K.G. Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient from 16.11.2024 to 08.12.2024 for a period of 23 days.

As per the wound certificate, petitioner has sustained one injury,
which is grievous in nature.

17. Punya Murthy C.P.- Medical Record officer at K.G. Hospital is examined as PW-2 and through him authorization letter, police intimation, MLC report and Inpatient case sheet are marked as Ex.P16 to Ex.P19.
18.

Dr.Shailesh A.V. Rao -Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bengaluru is examined as PW.3 and through him OPD record, Mini mental state examination report, CT brain report, Neuro Psychological assessment report, X-ray with report and CT scan film are got marked as per Ex.P20 to P25.
P.W.3 has deposed that petitioner has consulted him at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bangalore on 08.10.2025 and again on 10.10.2025 for the assessment of his disability.
The Pw3 further deposed that neuro psychological assessment of the petitioner was done on 09.10.2025.
His IQ was 95 (normal range 90-110.
On IDEAS, he obtained a score of 07, suggestive of 40-70% moderate disability.

PW.3 further deposed that MMSE was done to the petitioner on 08.10.2025, he obtained a score of 17/30 which is low score and Skull x-ray was done on 09.10.2025 and it revealed features of left parieto occipital and sub occipital craniotomy.
Bone flap seen in situ.

Pw.3 further deposed that petitioner has a power of around 4/5 in right upper limb and right lower limb and he has impaired memory and intelligence, his impaired hearing on left side and his slurred poor speech.
Pw.3 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent disability on whole body at 20%.
19. If the cross examination of PW.3 is perused, he has not given treatment to the petitioner.
He has assessed the disability after one year of the accident.
Except the discharge summary and wound certificate he has not verified any other medical documents at the time of his assessing the disability of the petitioner.
He has not even verified the follow up records to know whether petitioner has taken follow up treatment and if so, what kind of follow up treatment he has taken.
PW.3 pleaded ignorance of the IQ level of the petitioner prior to the accident.
Admittedly as per Ex.P3 the IQ level of the petitioner was normal at the time of assessing the disability.

Even though PW.3 has deposed that, the IDEAS score is less but, if the Ex.P23 is perused, wherein though in the conclusion portion it was opined that the IDEAS score is less, but in the same document at upper portion it was opined that, IDEAS score is adequate.
20.
As observed supra, PW.3 has assessed the Neuro - psychological disability of the petitioner at 20%.
21. If the evidence of PW.1 is perused, he has given rational answer to all the questions posed to him without any hindrance even for a while.
Further it is the petitioner himself has represented the case without his being represented through guardian.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has submitted that, the PW.3 has assessed the disability on higher side and the court can consider only 10% of the disability.

23. By considering the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner, the period of treatment taken and the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner and also considering the medical evidence it is just to assess the disability at 15% instead of 20%.
24.
Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
25. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.80,000/- towards pain and suffering.

26. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced Medical bills issued from K.G. Hospital for Rs.7,25,127/- and Medical bills for Rs.7,150/- at Ex.P11 and Ex.P26.
In all sum of Rs.7,32,277/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.7,32,277/-
27.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 60 years and he was working as Agriculture and earning Rs.35,000/- p.m.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence considering the age of petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
28.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment for 22 days as inpatient in K.G. Hospital.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of four months as complete laid down period.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.66,000/-
(16,500x4) towards loss of income during the laid down period.
29. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at K G Hospital.
Further for 22 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.50,000/-
taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
30. The petitioner has contended that he is aged about 60 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P12/Aadhar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 01-01-1964 that means he was aged about 60 years.
Hence considering the Aadhar Card this court has taken the age of petitioner as 60 years.

6 31.

sentences.text: So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,500/- p.m and by considering the evidence of PW.2 as he has assessed the disability on higher side this Court inclines to take the disability on whole body at 15% and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 60 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 is '9'.
So by applying the multiplier '9' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.2,67,300/- (i.e., Rs.16,500 x 15% x 9x12 )-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,67,300/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
32. The petitioner at his age of 60 years has suffered grievous injuries which definitely would have caused some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of comfort and amenities thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl. Heads Amount No.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.80,000/-
2.

Medical expenses Rs.7,32,277/-
3. Towards loss of income during Rs.66,000/-
 laid up period 4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs.50,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 5. Loss of future income Rs.2,67,300/-
6. Discomfort and amenities Rs.50,000/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.12,45,577/- (Rupees Twelve Lakh Forty Five Thousand Five Hundred Seventy Seven only)
33.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 1 st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.1 this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
34. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.12,45,577/- (Rupees Twelve Lakhs Forty Five Thousand Five Hundred Seventy Seven only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of Narayana Reddy vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90131886/
7 petition till the date of deposit.

sentences.text: The Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
